task: Independent visual cue-note audit for Corno II, Dvorak Symphony No. 8, movement 3

coordinate_frame.units: rendered pixels; approximate bounding boxes, not notehead centroids

method: Rendered source page at 300 dpi and visually inspected all 11 Corno II systems. Used printed source labels and reduced cue-note appearance; ranges are deliberately approximate. No source PDF, HTML, or score data was edited.

cue_groups.reason: Small high-register cue run sits immediately after the printed Viol. I. label; heads are visibly reduced and separate from the regular Horn II staff line.

systems.note: No separate instrument cue label or clearly reduced cue-note group observed.

cue_groups.reason: Short, ledgered small-note cue group immediately follows Vc., Cb.; visually distinct from the larger staff notation.

A second labeled cue is printed over the right-hand part of the system. Several small-looking heads align with this label, but the reduced heads merge with the staff and the Horn II line at this scan quality; verify against source before excluding any continuation beyond this box.

The repeated Tbe (D) label sits above a short right-side cue-like group. Heads are close to the main staff size in the scan, so the boundary is approximate; preserve as an audit candidate, not an unreviewed deletion.

cue_groups.reason: Ob. I. is printed beneath the staff near a note group. In this scan the noteheads do not separate cleanly by size from the Horn II notation, and the cue start/end cannot be established confidently.
Ob. appears over the opening note group; adjacent notes look close to normal size and the exact cue endpoint is not visually separable. Do not drop the full system as a cue based on this label alone.

use_guidance: Cue groups marked true can be excluded from Horn II playback. Groups marked review_before_excluding are cue-source candidates only; keep them out of generated audio only after checking notehead size/continuity against the original page, since their boundaries are uncertain.
audit_limitations: Coordinates are approximate page-image pixel bounds.
The scanned engraving blurs cue-size versus normal-size noteheads around Tbe (D), Ob. I., Ob., and the later Viol. I. label.
This audit identifies cue-source regions only; it does not transcribe pitch or duration.
